subject: Basic Digital Literacy
content: Spreadsheet software (Excel, Google Sheets) organizes data in rows and columns. Cells are intersections of rows (numbers) and columns (letters) - example A1. Enter data: text, numbers, formulas. Formulas start with = sign: =A1+B1 adds cells, =SUM(A1:A10) adds range, =AVERAGE(B1:B20) calculates mean. Formatting: bold headers, number formats (currency, percentage), borders, colors. Charts: select data, insert chart (bar, line, pie). Nigerian uses: tracking expenses, budgeting, grading students, sales records. Spreadsheets save time and reduce errors.
summary: Spreadsheets organize data in rows/columns. Cells (A1). Formulas start with =SUM, =AVERAGE. Charts visualize data. Excel, Google Sheets.

quiz_questions.question: What is a spreadsheet cell?
options: Intersection of row and column (e.g., A1)
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Intersection of row and column (e.g., A1)
quiz_questions.explanation: Cells are individual data entry points.

quiz_questions.question: What symbol starts a formula?
quiz_questions.explanation: Formulas begin with = sign.

quiz_questions.question: What does =SUM(A1:A10) do?
options: Adds all values in A1 to A10
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Adds all values in A1 to A10
quiz_questions.explanation: SUM calculates total.

quiz_questions.question: Which chart shows trends over time?
quiz_questions.explanation: Line charts connect data points to show change over time.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: Spreadsheets can only do simple addition.
quiz_questions.explanation: Spreadsheets can do complex calculations, statistics, and data analysis.

subject: Basic Digital Literacy
content: Presentation software (PowerPoint, Google Slides) creates slide shows for speaking. Best practices: one idea per slide, minimal text (6x6 rule - max 6 words per line, 6 lines per slide), readable fonts (sans-serif like Arial), high-contrast colors (dark text on light background), relevant images, consistent design. Use transitions and animations sparingly (don't distract). Rehearse timing. Nigerian students use presentations for class projects, reports, and debates. Include title slide, agenda, content slides, conclusion, and references. Practice speaking while presenting, not reading slides. Engage audience with questions.
summary: Presentation software: PowerPoint, Google Slides. One idea per slide, 6x6 rule (6 words/line, 6 lines). Readable fonts, high contrast, minimal animations.

quiz_questions.question: What is the 6x6 rule?
options: 6 words per line, 6 lines per slide
quiz_questions.correct_answer: 6 words per line, 6 lines per slide
quiz_questions.explanation: Limits text to keep slides readable.

quiz_questions.question: What font type is best for presentations?
quiz_questions.explanation: Sans-serif fonts are easier to read on screens.

quiz_questions.question: Should you read slides word-for-word?
options: No, talk naturally and use slides as cues
quiz_questions.correct_answer: No, talk naturally and use slides as cues
quiz_questions.explanation: Reading slides bores audiences. Speak naturally.

quiz_questions.question: What should be on a title slide?
quiz_questions.explanation: Title slide introduces the presentation.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: More animations make presentations better.
quiz_questions.explanation: Too many animations are distracting. Use sparingly.

subject: Basic Digital Literacy
content: Digital citizenship is responsible technology use. Nine elements: digital access (equal internet opportunity), digital commerce (online buying/selling legally), digital communication (respectful messaging), digital literacy (knowing how to use tech), digital etiquette (manners online), digital law (not stealing, hacking), digital rights/responsibilities (privacy, free speech), digital health/wellness (balance screen time, ergonomics), digital security (passwords, protection). Nigerian digital citizens: protect personal information, avoid cyberbullying, respect copyright (don't download illegal movies/music), think before posting, balance online/offline life, use strong passwords.
summary: Digital citizenship = responsible technology use. Nine elements: access, commerce, communication, literacy, etiquette, law, rights/responsibilities, health, security.

quiz_questions.question: What is digital citizenship?
quiz_questions.explanation: Digital citizenship covers rights, responsibilities, and safety online.

quiz_questions.question: Should you share your passwords with friends?
options: Never share with anyone except parents
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Never share with anyone except parents
quiz_questions.explanation: Passwords protect your accounts from unauthorized access.

quiz_questions.question: What is cyberbullying?
quiz_questions.explanation: Cyberbullying includes mean messages, spreading rumors, or excluding others online.

quiz_questions.question: Why respect copyright?
options: Creators deserve payment/credit, it's the law
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Creators deserve payment/credit, it's the law
quiz_questions.explanation: Illegal downloading hurts artists and is punishable.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: You can post anything online without consequences.
quiz_questions.explanation: Posts affect your reputation, friendships, and future opportunities.

subject: Basic Digital Literacy
content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the code for webpages. Tags are instructions inside angle brackets < >. Most tags have opening and closing . Basic structure: (entire page), (metadata, title), (tab name), <body> (visible content). Common tags: <h1> to <h6> (headings, h1 largest), <p> (paragraph), <img src='image.jpg'> (image), <a href='url'>link</a> (hyperlink), <ul><li>item</li></ul> (bullet list). Write HTML in any text editor, save as .html, open in browser. Nigerian students learn HTML in computer clubs to build simple webpages.
summary: HTML = code for webpages. Tags in < > brackets. Basic structure: html, head, title, body. Common tags: h1, p, img, a, ul/li.

quiz_questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
quiz_questions.explanation: HTML structures web content.

quiz_questions.question: What tag creates a paragraph?
quiz_questions.explanation: defines a paragraph.

quiz_questions.question: What does <a> tag do?
quiz_questions.explanation: <a> with href attribute creates hyperlinks.

quiz_questions.question: What extension saves HTML files?
quiz_questions.explanation: Browsers open .html files.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: HTML tags are case-sensitive.
quiz_questions.explanation: HTML tags can be uppercase or lowercase, but lowercase is standard.

subject: Basic Digital Literacy
content: Cybersecurity protects computers, networks, and data from attack. Common threats: malware (malicious software like viruses, worms, ransomware), phishing (fake emails tricking you to share info), hacking (unauthorized access), identity theft (stealing personal info). Protection: use antivirus software (Norton, Kaspersky, free Avast), enable firewalls, update software regularly (patches security holes), use strong unique passwords, enable two-factor authentication (2FA - requires code from phone), don't click suspicious links, backup important files. Nigerian cybersecurity agencies: NITDA, Nigeria Computer Emergency Response Team (ngCERT). Report cybercrime to police.
summary: Cybersecurity protects against threats: malware, phishing, hacking. Protection: antivirus, firewall, updates, strong passwords, 2FA. Report to ngCERT.

quiz_questions.question: What is malware?
quiz_questions.explanation: Malware damages or disables computers.

quiz_questions.question: What is phishing?
options: Fake emails tricking you to share info
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Fake emails tricking you to share info
quiz_questions.explanation: Phishing impersonates real companies to steal passwords or money.

quiz_questions.question: What does 2FA stand for?
quiz_questions.explanation: 2FA requires password plus code from phone for login.

quiz_questions.question: Why update software regularly?
quiz_questions.explanation: Updates patch vulnerabilities that hackers exploit.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: You only need cybersecurity on computers, not phones.
quiz_questions.explanation: Phones also need protection from malware and phishing.
